messages.content: How much time will it take for the light to reach earth from a star 4 light years away?

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

message.content:
A star that is 4 light‑years away will send its light to Earth in **about 4 years**.

**Why?**  
- A *light‑year* is defined as the distance that light travels in one year (≈9.46 × 10¹⁵ m).  
- Therefore, if a star is 4 light‑years away, the light has to cover 4 times that distance.  
- Since light travels at a constant speed of ~299 792 458 m/s, it takes exactly one year to cover one light‑year, so 4 light‑years → 4 years.

(If you wanted to express it in seconds:  
\(4 \text{ ly} \times 365.25 \text{ d/yr} \times 24 \text{ h/d} \times 3600 \text{ s/h} \approx 1.26 \times 10^8\) s.)
message.reasoning: We need to compute light travel time. The star is 4 light years away. Light travels at speed of light. So time = distance / speed. But distance is given in light years. Light year is the distance light travels in one year. So 4 light years means 4 years. So answer: 4 years.
